newsitem.title: INDONESIA: Indonesian president objects to broadcasting bill.
newsitem.headline: Indonesian president objects to broadcasting bill.

text.p: Indonesian President Suharto has asked parliament to re-examine the broadcasting bill passed last year because he feels some of the clauses are unworkable, the official Antara news agency reported on Thursday.

It quoted State Secretary Murdiono as telling a parliamentary commission on Wednesday that Suharto had made the unprecedented move to ask a passed bill to be reconsidered because a number of items in the bill were hard to implement.
"Even though the parliament passed the bill several months ago, the president is not yet prepared to sign it," Murdiono said.
"To the president, this is a matter of principle because it would be a mistake for him to sign a bill into law that contains matters which are technically hard to implement," Murdiono said.
He said the president would write to the parliament's leaders soon to consider holding discussions with the government on a number of articles in the bill.

The Jakarta Post newspaper quoted Information Minister Hartono as saying another government concern with the bill was that the ministry issues operational licences for broadcasters on a five-yearly basis.

"The term is too short, because the broadcasting business deals with big investment. I think the licences should ideally apply for at least 10 years," said Hartono, who retired as army chief of staff last month before taking up his new post.
He said the bill's provisions for punitive measures were also likely to be amended.

The broadcasting bill is the nation's first law of its type and is aimed at protecting the domestic broadcasting industry as well as extending the law to cable television and other new multi-media technologies.
The bill had originally been submitted to parliament in March last year and was finally passed by parliament in December.
